items.title: The UN System — Organs, Council & Reform
items.body:
### The United Nations and its organs

**In one line**
The United Nations is the world's main body for peace, development and law, run through six principal organs, and the exam tests its founding date, its organs, who heads them and the reform debate.

**Why it is asked**
Almost every prelims paper has one UN question — a date, an organ's seat, the current Secretary-General, or whether the Trusteeship Council is still active (a classic trap).

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
After the Second World War, 50 states met at San Francisco and the **UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945** to prevent another world war. The UN set up **six principal organs** to share the work: a plenary **General Assembly** of all members, a **Security Council** for peace and security, **ECOSOC** to coordinate economic and social work, a **Secretariat** to administer, the **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** at The Hague for disputes between states, and the **Trusteeship Council** to oversee former colonies — which finished its job and **suspended operations in 1994** after Palau became independent.

**Picture it (the six organs)**

| Organ | Seat / role |
|---|---|
| General Assembly | Plenary of all 193 members, New York |
| Security Council | Peace and security; 15 members |
| ECOSOC | Coordinates 15+ specialised agencies |
| Secretariat | Administrative arm under the Secretary-General |
| ICJ | Principal judicial organ, The Hague (15 judges elected for nine-year terms) |
| Trusteeship Council | Suspended since 1994 (not active) |

**Four specialised agencies the exam matches**

| Agency | Headquarters | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| WHO | Geneva | Global public health |
| ILO | Geneva | Labour standards |
| UNESCO | Paris | Education, science and culture |
| FAO | Rome | Food and agriculture |

WHO and ILO share Geneva, so a match question may pair each agency with its city **and** its focus.

**The Security Council and reform**
The UNSC has **15 members = 5 permanent (P5) + 10 non-permanent** (two-year terms, elected by the General Assembly). The **P5 — USA, UK, France, Russia, China** — each hold the **veto**. Because this reflects 1945, not today, the **G4 (India, Japan, Germany, Brazil)** press for new permanent seats and Africa demands two through the **Ezulwini Consensus**. India is a strong claimant but **not yet** a permanent member.

**Terms explained**
- **Veto** — the power of any P5 member to block a substantive Security Council decision.
- **ECOSOC** — Economic and Social Council, which coordinates the UN's specialised agencies.
- **Ezulwini Consensus** — the African Union's common position demanding two permanent (with veto) and extra non-permanent UNSC seats.
- **Secretary-General** — the UN's chief administrative officer: **António Guterres** (Portugal), in office since January 2017, with his second term running to the end of 2026; appointed by the General Assembly on the Security Council's recommendation.

**Don't confuse**
- The **ICJ** (UN organ, state disputes, The Hague) vs the **ICC** (International Criminal Court — tries individuals, also at The Hague but **not** a UN organ).
- The Trusteeship Council still legally exists but is **inactive** since 1994 — it is not a 'currently operating' organ.

**Remember it**
G4 seat-seekers spell **'JBIG'** → Japan, Brazil, India, Germany.

**TL;DR**
- UN founded 24 October 1945; HQ New York; 193 members; six principal organs.
- Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 — not currently active.
- UNSC = 5 permanent (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) + 10 non-permanent (2-year terms).
- G4 = India, Japan, Germany, Brazil seek permanent UNSC seats; India is not yet permanent.
- António Guterres (Portugal) has been UN Secretary-General since January 2017.
- HQs: WHO and ILO Geneva, UNESCO Paris, FAO Rome, ICJ The Hague (President Yuji Iwasawa, Japan).
keyPoints: UN founded 24 October 1945; HQ New York; 193 members; six principal organs.
Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 — not currently active.
UNSC = 5 permanent (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) + 10 non-permanent (2-year terms).
G4 = India, Japan, Germany, Brazil seek permanent UNSC seats; India is not yet a permanent member.
António Guterres (Portugal) has been UN Secretary-General since January 2017.
HQs: WHO & ILO Geneva, UNESCO Paris, FAO Rome, ICJ The Hague (President Yuji Iwasawa, Japan).

items.title: Bretton Woods Twins & the WTO
items.body:
### The IMF, the World Bank and the WTO

**In one line**
The IMF, the World Bank (the 'Bretton Woods twins') and the WTO are the three pillars of the global economic order, each with a fixed headquarters and a current head the exam asks about.

**Why it is asked**
Statement and match questions test the 1944 Bretton Woods origin, which arm is 'the World Bank', the Washington/Geneva headquarters, and the names of the current MD/President/DG.

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
In July 1944, with the war ending, 44 nations met at **Bretton Woods** (New Hampshire, USA) to rebuild a stable world economy, creating two 'twins': the **IMF** to keep currencies and balance-of-payments stable, and the **World Bank** to lend for reconstruction and development — both based in **Washington, D.C.** Trade was meant to have a third body, but that failed in 1948; the gap was filled by the **GATT**, which finally became the **World Trade Organization on 1 January 1995**, headquartered in **Geneva**, this time with a **binding dispute-settlement** system.

**Picture it (the three pillars)**

| Body | Born | HQ | Head (Oct 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMF | 1944 | Washington, D.C. | Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria) |
| World Bank | 1944 | Washington, D.C. | Ajay Banga (Indian-American) |
| WTO | 1995 (from GATT) | Geneva | Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria) |

**The five arms of the World Bank Group**

| Arm | Role |
|---|---|
| IBRD | Loans to middle-income governments |
| IDA | Concessional credit to the poorest states |
| IFC | Private-sector financing |
| MIGA | Political-risk guarantees |
| ICSID | Investment dispute settlement |

**'IBRD + IDA = the World Bank.'** By an old convention the **IMF MD is European** and the **World Bank President is American**.

**Terms explained**
- **Balance-of-payments support** — emergency lending the IMF gives a country that cannot pay for its imports or debts.
- **Concessional credit (IDA)** — loans at little or no interest for the poorest countries.
- **Binding dispute settlement** — WTO rulings that members must obey, unlike the old GATT's weaker system.

**Don't confuse**
- **IMF** (short-term monetary stability) vs **World Bank** (long-term development lending) — both at Washington.
- The **WTO** is at **Geneva**, not Washington; the IMF/World Bank are the Bretton Woods pair, not the WTO.

**Remember it**
World Bank arms spell **'I-I-I-M-I'** = IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID.

**TL;DR**
- IMF and World Bank were both born at Bretton Woods (1944), HQ Washington, D.C.
- IMF Managing Director = Kristalina Georgieva; World Bank President = Ajay Banga.
- World Bank = IBRD + IDA; the Group also has IFC, MIGA, ICSID.
- WTO replaced GATT on 1 January 1995; HQ Geneva; has binding dispute settlement.
- WTO Director-General = Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria), first woman and first African in the post.
keyPoints: IMF and World Bank were both born at Bretton Woods (1944), HQ Washington D.C.
IMF Managing Director = Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria); World Bank President = Ajay Banga.
World Bank = IBRD + IDA; the Group also has IFC (private sector), MIGA (guarantees), ICSID (disputes).
WTO replaced GATT on 1 January 1995; HQ Geneva; has binding dispute settlement.
WTO Director-General = Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria), first woman and first African to hold the post.
items.mnemonic: World Bank arms 'I-I-I-M-I' = IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID.
items.source: IMF (imf.org); World Bank (worldbank.org); WTO (wto.org) — verified Oct 2026

items.title: Multilateral Development Banks — ADB, AIIB, NDB
items.body:
### The three development banks India belongs to

**In one line**
The ADB, AIIB and NDB are regional development banks that lend for infrastructure; India is a founding member of all three, and the exam separates them by founding year, headquarters and current head.

**Why it is asked**
Match-the-HQ questions mix up Beijing (AIIB) and Shanghai (NDB), and office-holder questions test the latest presidents — which change often.

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
In **1966** Asia set up the **ADB** in **Manila** to fund the region's development, led by convention by a Japanese national. Decades later China, wanting more say in development finance, launched the **AIIB** (operational **2016**) in **Beijing** for infrastructure. Separately the BRICS countries created their own bank — the **New Development Bank (NDB)** — by the Fortaleza Declaration (2014), operational 2015, in **Shanghai**, to reduce dependence on the Western-led Bretton Woods bodies.

**Picture it (bank → founded → HQ → head)**

| Bank | Founded | HQ | Head (Oct 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADB | 1966 | Manila | Masato Kanda (Japan) |
| AIIB | 2016 | Beijing | Zou Jiayi (China) |
| NDB | 2014/15 | Shanghai | Dilma Rousseff (Brazil) |

**Terms explained**
- **Multilateral development bank** — a bank owned by many member governments that lends for development, especially infrastructure.
- **BRICS bank** — the informal name for the NDB, created by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.
- **Rotating presidency** — the NDB's top job passes among its founding members.

**Current heads (verify each exam cycle)**
- **ADB — Masato Kanda** (since February 2025, succeeding Masatsugu Asakawa); the ADB President is always Japanese by convention.
- **AIIB — Zou Jiayi** (since January 2026, succeeding founding President **Jin Liqun**).
- **NDB — Dilma Rousseff** (former Brazilian President), since 2023; new NDB members include Egypt, the UAE and Bangladesh.

**Don't confuse**
- **AIIB = Beijing**, **NDB = Shanghai** — both are China-hosted, but only the NDB is the BRICS bank.
- The **ADB** (1966) is the oldest and is Manila-based, not China-based: it **was established in 1966 and is headquartered in Manila, Philippines**.
- The **IMF** and the **World Bank** are not regional banks; both are headquartered in **Washington D.C.** — a frequent extra item in HQ match questions.

**Remember it**
'**ADB-Manila, AIIB-Beijing, NDB-Shanghai**' — oldest to newest, moving east within China for the two Chinese-hosted banks.

**TL;DR**
- ADB founded 1966, HQ Manila; President (always Japanese) is Masato Kanda since Feb 2025.
- AIIB operational 2016, HQ Beijing; President Zou Jiayi succeeded founding head Jin Liqun in Jan 2026.
- NDB is the BRICS bank, HQ Shanghai; President Dilma Rousseff since 2023.
- AIIB and NDB are both China-hosted but distinct — only the NDB is the BRICS bank.
- India is a founding member of ADB, AIIB and NDB.
keyPoints: ADB founded 1966, HQ Manila; President (always Japanese) is Masato Kanda since Feb 2025.
AIIB operational 2016, HQ Beijing; President Zou Jiayi succeeded founding head Jin Liqun in Jan 2026.
NDB is the BRICS bank, HQ Shanghai; President Dilma Rousseff since 2023.
AIIB and NDB are both China-hosted but distinct — only the NDB is the BRICS bank.
India is a founding member of ADB, AIIB and NDB.

items.title: Regional & Plurilateral Groupings + Export-Control Regimes
items.body:
### Regional bodies, plurilateral clubs and export regimes

**In one line**
This note sorts the alphabet-soup of regional organisations (SAARC, ASEAN, BIMSTEC, EU), the plurilateral clubs India joins (G20, BRICS, SCO, QUAD), and the four export-control regimes — by headquarters, year and India's status.

**Why it is asked**
These are pure match-and-recall items: HQ pairs, which club India is or is not in, and the exact years India joined the export regimes.

**The story (why so many bodies)**
Countries group by geography (SAARC, ASEAN) or by shared interest across regions (G20, BRICS). India uses both: it leads its South Asian neighbourhood while also sitting in global economic clubs, so examiners test whether you can keep the memberships straight.

**Picture it — regional organisations**

| Body | Founded | HQ | Members |
|---|---|---|---|
| SAARC | 1985 | Kathmandu | 8 |
| ASEAN | 1967 | Jakarta | 11 (Timor-Leste joined 2025) |
| BIMSTEC | 1997 | Dhaka | 7 |
| EU | 1993 | Brussels | 27 |

**Plurilateral groupings (India's role)**
- **G20**: India held the **presidency in 2023 (New Delhi Declaration)**, where the **African Union was admitted as a permanent member**. **G7** is a separate advanced-economy club (India is not a member).
- **BRICS**: expanded from 2024 (added **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE**; **Indonesia** joined in 2025) to ten members.
- **SCO**: India became a **full member in 2017**; HQ Beijing.
- **QUAD**: India, USA, Japan, Australia. **I2U2**: India, Israel, UAE, USA.

**Export-control regimes (India's status)**

| Regime | India joined |
|---|---|
| MTCR | 2016 |
| Wassenaar Arrangement | 2017 |
| Australia Group | 2018 |
| NSG | Bid blocked (China objects, NPT issue) |

**Climate fora:** the **UNFCCC (1992)** is the climate treaty; the **Paris Agreement (2015)** sits under it; the **IPCC** (set up by **WMO + UNEP**) provides the scientific assessments.

**Terms explained**
- **Plurilateral** — a club of several (but not all) countries cooperating by shared interest rather than region.
- **Export-control regime** — a voluntary group of states that agree rules on trading sensitive missile, dual-use, chemical-biological or nuclear items.
- **UNFCCC / IPCC** — the UN climate treaty, and the independent scientific panel that advises on climate; the IPCC is **not** under the UNFCCC.

**Don't confuse**
- **SAARC = Kathmandu** vs **BIMSTEC = Dhaka** — the exam swaps these two Bay-of-Bengal-area HQs.
- India is in **MTCR, Wassenaar and Australia Group** but **not** the **NSG**.
- The **IPCC** was created by **WMO and UNEP**, not by the UNFCCC.

**Remember it**
India's export-club years run **16 → 17 → 18** (MTCR-2016, Wassenaar-2017, Australia Group-2018); NSG still pending.

**TL;DR**
- HQs: SAARC Kathmandu, ASEAN Jakarta, BIMSTEC Dhaka, EU Brussels.
- India held the G20 presidency in 2023; the African Union became a permanent G20 member at New Delhi.
- India became a full SCO member in 2017; QUAD = India, USA, Japan, Australia; I2U2 = India, Israel, UAE, USA.
- India joined MTCR (2016), Wassenaar (2017) and Australia Group (2018) but NOT the NSG.
- IPCC was established by WMO and UNEP; the Paris Agreement (2015) operates under the UNFCCC (1992).
keyPoints: HQs: SAARC Kathmandu, ASEAN Jakarta, BIMSTEC Dhaka, EU Brussels.
India held the G20 presidency in 2023; the African Union became a permanent G20 member at the New Delhi summit.
India became a full SCO member in 2017; QUAD = India, USA, Japan, Australia; I2U2 = India, Israel, UAE, USA.
India joined MTCR (2016), Wassenaar (2017) and Australia Group (2018) but NOT the NSG.
IPCC was established by WMO and UNEP; the Paris Agreement (2015) operates under the UNFCCC (1992).
items.mnemonic: India's export-club years: MTCR-16, Wassenaar-17, Australia Group-18 (16→17→18), NSG still pending.
items.source: MEA (mea.gov.in); SAARC/ASEAN/BIMSTEC/EU sites; IPCC (ipcc.ch); UNFCCC (unfccc.int) — verified Oct 2026

items.title: PYQ Precision — Reports, Memberships, HQs & OECD
items.body:
### Precision facts: reports, memberships and headquarters

**In one line**
A quick-reference of the 'which body publishes this report', 'is India a member', and 'which city hosts this agency' facts that previous-year questions test most often.

**Why it is asked**
These are recall traps where one wrong pairing (WHO in Vienna, India in the OECD) flips the whole answer, so exact knowledge beats reasoning.

**The story (why the traps work)**
Many reports have similar grand names and many agencies cluster in the same cities (Geneva, Vienna, Rome), so examiners build match questions hoping you confuse them. The tables below fix the pairings.

**Picture it — 'report published by'**

| Report | Body |
|---|---|
| Human Development Report | UNDP |
| World Investment Report | UNCTAD |
| Global Competitiveness Report | WEF (non-UN, Davos) |
| Global Financial Stability Report / World Economic Outlook | IMF |
| World Development Report | World Bank |
| State of World Population | UNFPA |

**India: member vs not**

| India IS a member | India is NOT a member |
|---|---|
| UN, IMF, World Bank, WTO, ADB, AIIB (Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank; 2nd-largest shareholder), NDB | OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, Paris), OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, Vienna), ICSID |

**HQ clusters (traps)**

| City | Bodies |
|---|---|
| Vienna | IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency), OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries), UNIDO, CTBTO |
| Geneva | WHO, ILO, WTO, WMO, WIPO |
| Rome | FAO, WFP, IFAD |
| Nairobi | UNEP, UN-Habitat |
| The Hague | ICJ and ICC |

**Terms explained**
- **BEPS** — Base Erosion and Profit Shifting: the OECD/G20 framework against tax avoidance, underpinning the **Two-Pillar** global minimum corporate tax (**15%**).
- **TFA** — the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, concluded at the Bali Ministerial (2013).
- **Masala bonds** — rupee-denominated bonds issued outside India by the International Finance Corporation (IFC, a World Bank Group arm), which pioneered them, and by others.

**Don't confuse**
- World Investment Report = **UNCTAD**, but Global Competitiveness Report = **WEF** — the exam swaps these two.
- India is **not** in the **OECD** or **OPEC**, but **is** a founding member of the **AIIB**.

**Remember it**
'**Vienna = atoms and oil (IAEA, OPEC); Geneva = health, labour, trade (WHO, ILO, WTO)**'.

**TL;DR**
- HDR = UNDP; World Investment Report = UNCTAD; Global Competitiveness Report = WEF; GFSR/WEO = IMF.
- India is NOT in the OECD or OPEC, but IS in AIIB, NDB, ADB, IMF, World Bank and WTO.
- Vienna hosts IAEA and OPEC; Geneva hosts WHO/ILO/WTO; Rome hosts FAO.
- BEPS is the OECD/G20 framework; the Two-Pillar deal sets a 15% global minimum tax.
- The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement was agreed at Bali (2013); Masala bonds are offshore rupee bonds (IFC).
keyPoints: HDR = UNDP; World Investment Report = UNCTAD; Global Competitiveness Report = WEF (non-UN); GFSR/WEO = IMF.
India is NOT a member of the OECD or OPEC, but IS a member of AIIB, NDB, ADB, IMF, World Bank and WTO.
Vienna hosts IAEA and OPEC; Geneva hosts WHO/ILO/WTO; Rome hosts FAO.
BEPS is the OECD/G20 framework; the Two-Pillar deal sets a 15% global minimum tax.
The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement was agreed at Bali (2013); Masala bonds are offshore rupee bonds (IFC).

items.title: The UN System in Full — Charter, Organs, Agencies, Headquarters and Heads (October 2026)
items.body:
## How the UN was built and who runs its agencies

**In one line:** the **UN Charter** was signed at **San Francisco** on **26 June 1945** and came into force on **24 October 1945**; the UN works through six organs and some **15 specialised agencies**, each with its own HQ and head.

**Why it is asked:** founding years, HQ cities and current heads are the commonest UN items, and 2026 is a year of change at the top.

**The story**

### Founding and organs
- The Charter was signed by **50** states at San Francisco on **26 June 1945**; with Poland there were **51 original members** — **India** among them. It entered into force on **24 October 1945** (**UN Day**); the UN marked its **80th anniversary** in **2025**.
- **193** members; the newest is **South Sudan** (**2011**).
- The **Security Council** grew from **11** to **15** members by an amendment in force in **1965**.
- **ECOSOC** has **54** members elected for three years.
- The **ICJ** has **15** judges with **nine-year** terms; India's **Dalveer Bhandari** sits on it (re-elected 2017).
- **Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit** was the first woman **President of the General Assembly** (**1953**).
- **Secretary-General António Guterres**'s second term ends on **31 December 2026**; the race for his successor was still open in **October 2026**.
- **UN High Commissioner for Human Rights:** **Volker Türk**, given a new term in **July 2026**.

### Specialised agencies and programmes
| Body | Founded | HQ | Head (October 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ILO** | **1919** (oldest; Nobel Peace Prize **1969**) | Geneva | **Gilbert Houngbo** (Togo) |
| **FAO** | **16 October 1945** (World Food Day) | Rome | **Qu Dongyu** (China) |
| **UNESCO** | **16 November 1945** | Paris | **Khaled El-Enany** (Egypt), since November 2025 |
| **WHO** | **7 April 1948** (World Health Day) | Geneva | **Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus** (Ethiopia) |
| **IAEA** | **1957** | Vienna | **Rafael Grossi** (Argentina) |
| **UNICEF** | 1946 | New York | **Catherine Russell** (USA) |

**Other HQs:** **UNHCR**, **WIPO**, **ITU** — Geneva; **UPU** — **Bern**; **ICAO** — **Montreal**; **IMO** — **London**; **UNEP** and **UN-Habitat** — **Nairobi**; **WFP** and **IFAD** — Rome; **UNIDO** — Vienna; **UN Tourism** — **Madrid**; **UNDP** and **UNFPA** — New York.

## Don't confuse
- **UPU** is in **Bern**, not Geneva; **ICAO** is in **Montreal**, not New York.
- **ILO (1919)** is older than the UN itself.

**TL;DR**
- Charter signed 26 June 1945 (50 states; 51 original members incl. India); in force 24 October 1945; 193 members; South Sudan newest.
- UNSC 11 → 15 (1965); ECOSOC 54; ICJ 15 judges, Dalveer Bhandari; Pandit first woman PGA (1953); Guterres to 31 December 2026.
- ILO 1919 Houngbo; FAO Qu Dongyu; UNESCO El-Enany; WHO Tedros; IAEA Grossi; UPU Bern; ICAO Montreal.
keyPoints: The UN Charter was signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945 by 50 states (51 original members, including India) and came into force on 24 October 1945; the UN turned 80 in 2025.
The UN has 193 members, the newest being South Sudan (2011); the Security Council grew from 11 to 15 members in 1965; ECOSOC has 54 members.
India's Dalveer Bhandari is an ICJ judge; Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was the first woman President of the General Assembly (1953).
Guterres's term ends on 31 December 2026 and the race for the next Secretary-General was open in October 2026; Volker Türk got a new term as human-rights chief in July 2026.
Heads: ILO Gilbert Houngbo, FAO Qu Dongyu, UNESCO Khaled El-Enany (since November 2025), WHO Tedros, IAEA Rafael Grossi, UNICEF Catherine Russell.
ILO (1919) is the oldest agency; UPU is at Bern, ICAO at Montreal, IMO at London, UNEP and UN-Habitat at Nairobi, UN Tourism at Madrid.
items.source: UN Charter and un.org; agency websites (WHO, ILO, UNESCO, FAO, IAEA, IMF, World Bank, WTO, ASEAN, BIMSTEC, IORA, ISA); NCERT Class XII Contemporary World Politics Ch. 6 (International Organisations); PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/pol-international-institutions.md; current items verified on the web (UN News, ASEAN portal, AIR, The Hindu, Business Standard), 18 Oct 2026

items.title: Economic, Regional & India-Led Bodies in Full — IMF, WTO, ASEAN, BIMSTEC, IORA, ISA (October 2026)
items.body:
## Money, trade, regions and India's own initiatives

**In one line:** beyond the UN, the exam asks about the **IMF and WTO** rules, **regional bodies** (ASEAN, SAARC, BIMSTEC, IORA), **clubs** India is not in (OECD, OPEC, G7) and the bodies **India founded** (ISA, CDRI).

**Why it is asked:** membership counts, latest summits and India-hosted HQs (Gurugram, New Delhi) are easy marks.

**The story**

### Money and trade
- **IMF:** **191** members; the **SDR** basket has five currencies — US dollar, euro, **Chinese renminbi** (added **2016**), yen and pound.
- **World Bank Group:** **MIGA** (**1988**) gives guarantees; **ICSID** (**1966**) settles investment disputes — **India is not a member** of ICSID.
- **WTO:** **166** members; DG **Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala** began a **second term** on **1 September 2025**; **Doha Round** launched **2001**; the **Trade Facilitation Agreement** came into force on **22 February 2017**; the **Appellate Body** has not worked since **December 2019**; ministerials — **MC13 Abu Dhabi (2024)**, **MC14 Yaoundé, Cameroon (2026)**.
- **OECD** — **38** members, Paris; **OPEC** — founded at **Baghdad** in **1960**, HQ Vienna. India is in **neither**.
- **G7 2026** summit at **Evian**, France (**15-17 June 2026**); PM Modi attended as a guest.

### Regional bodies
| Body | Key facts (October 2026) |
|---|---|
| **ASEAN** | **11** members since **Timor-Leste** was admitted on **26 October 2025**; **Philippines** chairs in **2026** |
| **SAARC** | Founded at **Dhaka** in **1985**; **8** members; the last summit was the **18th (Kathmandu, 2014)** — the 2016 Islamabad summit was cancelled |
| **BIMSTEC** | **Bangkok Declaration, 1997**; **7** members; its **Charter** came into force in **2024**; **6th summit** at **Bangkok** (April 2025); Secretary-General **Indra Mani Pandey** (India) |
| **IORA** | **1997**; Secretariat at **Ebene, Mauritius**; **India chairs** for **2025-27** |
| **Commonwealth** | **56** members; Secretary-General **Shirley Botchwey** (Ghana); London |

### Law, climate and India-led bodies
- **ICC** (International Criminal Court) — **Rome Statute, 1998**; India is **not** a member. **Interpol** — HQ **Lyon**.
- **UNFCCC COP30** — **Belém**, Brazil (2025); **COP31** — **Antalya**, Türkiye, **9-20 November 2026**.
- **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** — launched by **India and France** at **Paris** on **30 November 2015**; HQ **Gurugram**.
- **Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)** — **2019**; HQ **New Delhi**.
- **Global Biofuels Alliance** — launched at the **G20 New Delhi** summit (**2023**).

### Andhra Pradesh and multilateral lenders
- For **Amaravati**, the **World Bank** approved **$800 million** and the **ADB** **$788.8 million** in **December 2024**; the World Bank released **$340 million** in **April 2026**.

## Don't confuse
- **ISA** is at **Gurugram**; **CDRI** at **New Delhi**.
- **SAARC** was founded at **Dhaka** but its Secretariat is at **Kathmandu**; **BIMSTEC**'s Secretariat is at **Dhaka**.

**TL;DR**
- IMF 191, SDR five currencies (renminbi 2016); India not in ICSID; WTO 166, MC14 Yaoundé 2026; OECD 38; OPEC Baghdad 1960.
- ASEAN 11 (Timor-Leste 2025); SAARC 1985, last summit 2014; BIMSTEC Charter 2024; India chairs IORA 2025-27.
- ICC 1998 (India out); COP31 Antalya; ISA Gurugram (2015); CDRI New Delhi (2019); Amaravati loans $800m + $788.8m.
keyPoints: The IMF has 191 members; the SDR basket has five currencies, the Chinese renminbi added in 2016; India is not a member of ICSID.
The WTO has 166 members; Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala began her second term on 1 September 2025; MC13 was at Abu Dhabi (2024) and MC14 at Yaoundé (2026); the Appellate Body has been idle since December 2019.
OPEC was founded at Baghdad in 1960 (HQ Vienna); the OECD has 38 members; the 2026 G7 summit was at Evian, France.
Timor-Leste became ASEAN's 11th member on 26 October 2025; SAARC's last summit was the 18th at Kathmandu (2014); the BIMSTEC Charter came into force in 2024.
India chairs IORA for 2025-27 (Secretariat at Ebene, Mauritius); the Commonwealth has 56 members under Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey.
The ISA (India-France, 30 November 2015) is at Gurugram and CDRI (2019) at New Delhi; COP31 is at Antalya; the World Bank ($800 million) and ADB ($788.8 million) fund Amaravati.

items.title: For Mains — International Institutions, Agencies & Fora
items.body:
### For Mains — reform and relevance of global institutions

**In one line**
For Mains, argue that the post-1945 institutions are losing legitimacy in a multipolar world, and that India (and the Global South) are building parallel bodies while pressing for reform.

**The dimensions Mains asks**

| Dimension | What to write |
|---|---|
| Why reform is needed | UNSC frozen at 1945; Bretton Woods quota under-weights emerging economies |
| India's demand | Permanent UNSC seat (G4), IMF quota reform, 'reformed multilateralism' |
| New architecture | BRICS NDB, AIIB, Contingent Reserve Arrangement — alternatives to Western-led bodies |
| Effectiveness | Veto paralysis (Ukraine, Gaza), WTO Appellate Body deadlock, climate-finance shortfalls |
| Criticism / limits | New banks still small; reform resisted by incumbents; Global South not monolithic |
| Way forward | 'Reformed multilateralism', expand UNSC, deliver climate finance, G20 as bridge |

**Data points / bodies to quote**
- UNSC: 5 permanent + 10 non-permanent since 1965; no structural reform since.
- G20 New Delhi Declaration (2023) and the African Union's permanent seat.
- NDB (Shanghai, Dilma Rousseff) and AIIB (Beijing, Zou Jiayi from 2026) as new finance.
- WTO dispute-settlement (Appellate Body) crisis; TFA (Bali 2013) as a success.
- OECD/G20 Two-Pillar 15% global minimum tax — rule-making beyond the UN.

**The AP angle**
Andhra Pradesh is a large recipient of multilateral project finance — ADB and World Bank fund Amaravati capital works, Visakhapatnam urban and port projects, and polavaram-linked irrigation support — showing how these institutions touch state development directly.

**Use in answers**
- Example: cite the AU's G20 admission (2023) as India delivering 'reformed multilateralism'.
- Quote: India's call for the UN to reflect 'the realities of the 21st century, not 1945'.
- Diagram idea: two columns — 'Old order (UN, IMF, World Bank)' vs 'New order (NDB, AIIB, BRICS+)' with India bridging both.
keyPoints: Frame it as a legitimacy crisis of 1945-era institutions in a multipolar world.
India's asks: permanent UNSC seat (G4), IMF quota reform, 'reformed multilateralism'.
New architecture: NDB and AIIB as Global-South alternatives to Bretton Woods bodies.
Effectiveness gaps: UNSC veto paralysis, WTO Appellate Body deadlock, climate-finance shortfalls.
AP angle: ADB/World Bank finance Amaravati, Visakhapatnam and irrigation projects in the state.
items.source: MEA; UN; World Bank/ADB project data (analysis, verified Oct 2026)
